avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 induction reduces mexiletine levels and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if patient requires St. John's Wort, obtain baseline and repeat mexiletine levels after 2-3 weeks

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Seed Extract
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases mexiletine plasma concentrations and toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice entirely; counsel patient on hidden sources in supplements

caution_supplements.name: Garlic Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP1A2 induction may modestly reduce mexiletine levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for loss of arrhythmia control; consider mexiletine level monitoring if high-dose garlic supplement used

caution_supplements.name: Flaxseed
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have modest CYP1A2 inducing properties
caution_supplements.action: Monitor clinical response; use established brands with consistent composition

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition significantly increases mexiletine bioavailability and plasma concentrations, elevating toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Strictly avoid; counsel patient and family members; check dietary supplements and juices for grapefruit content

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages (coffee, tea, energy drinks)
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine competes for CYP1A2 metabolism; high intake may increase mexiletine levels slightly
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent caffeine intake; counsel patient to avoid sudden increases; monitor for tremor or palpitations

caution_foods.name: Charbroiled/smoked foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons may induce CYP1A2, potentially reducing mexiletine levels
caution_foods.action: Counsel on moderation; maintain consistent dietary patterns; monitor arrhythmia control

caution_foods.name: Acidic foods (citrus, vinegar, tomatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Acidic environment increases mexiletine reabsorption in renal tubules, potentially raising serum levels
caution_foods.action: Counsel on maintaining neutral urinary pH; avoid extreme dietary acid loads; monitor for toxicity signs

monitoring_notes: Mexiletine has a narrow therapeutic window (0.5-2 μg/mL); obtain baseline level within 3-5 days of initiation or dose changes, then at steady-state (5-7 days). Monitor for tremor, dizziness, nausea, and arrhythmia recurrence, especially with CYP enzyme-inducing or -inhibiting interactions; renal function and urinary pH significantly influence mexiletine elimination and require assessment.
